note: What each update brings, in plain words for Joshua. One line per change that reaches the Mac, newest last, each with a kind: major (a big change: new major version and a new name), feature (bumps the middle number) or fix (the last number). Keep each line short (under 10 words) and plain: no tech words.

items.text: Your browser is now called Samara.
Only one Samara in your Dock.
Updates get ready in the background. No more freezing.
Each update has a number and a name.
The Update button glows when an update is ready.
Big updates get a new name.
Aang can tell you what each update brought.
Your logins are no longer saved in a sync file.
A new update window with tick boxes.
The Update button changes color the longer you wait.
Skipping an update asks you twice.
You can go back a version, or update overnight.
Check for updates is in Samara's menu.
New lantern icon: lit when open, dark when closed.
The lantern fades on and off smoothly.
Restarting for an update takes seconds.
Claude asks you first before using Samara.
Claude asks before sending your details anywhere.
Web pages can't trick Claude into pressing Send.
AI can never open your bank sites.

Claude can read your tabs, but only if you say yes.

Shops and PayPal checkouts work as normal.
Claude can't see hidden trick text on pages.
Web pages can't reach your home network.

ALL MOCKUPS in the trail opens your quest log.

Samara updates itself from GitHub on both computers.

Samara notes crashes and frozen pages in its log.

Claude's mark turns with Aang at every edge.

Claude and Aang can picture Samara's whole window.
Aang decides when to speak the same on both computers.

Claude's plan cards reach Aang's bubble on the Mac.
Pop-out videos on the Mac skip ads too.

Aang asks his AI one steady way, with time limits.
Aang keeps one list of your Claude sessions.
Your settings and lists save safely, even in a power cut.

Claude's page reads are shorter, so they cost less.

Claude opens and searches a page in one step.

Claude's reads of one part of a page are short too.
Updates show up within minutes, even after sleep or a Wi-Fi change.
Claude's page search no longer mixes up items in a list.
Claude can look at a tab that was asleep or still loading.

Take over a tab while Claude drives it.

Hand back with a note; Claude hears what changed.

The browser is called Samara everywhere.
Aang's notes go to the right folder on each machine.

Mockups: new ones sit in their own New section.
Mockups: search by name or number, filter by mark, sort newest.
Aang's Mac app updates itself with his brain, and is running again after every update.
A new engine is signed for Netflix and Prime on each machine before it is offered.

Claude's tabs are real tabs you can click into.
Take over one tab; Claude keeps working in the others.
Drag a tab out of Claude's group to keep it.
After STOP ALL, Claude can start again in the same chat.
Claude can update Aang right away when you ask, without waiting for you to step away.
Claude can tick hidden boxes and choices on forms.
No more asking when Claude only moves through a page.
Words in your essays no longer look like buying.
A Samara restart never locks Claude out of its chat.
Claude's tabs and your typing come back after a restart, and the same chat carries on.

Aang sounds warmer and more like himself, Discord too.
Aang's replies finish sooner, no extra wait at the end.
Small talk and simple questions answered instantly on your PC.
Snips you ask about are read instantly on your PC.
Claude's mockups always reach Samara, even without Aang.
